summary: A whole dashboard screen from a list of cards: one column on a phone (stacked, scrolling), two on a landscape phone or small tablet, three or four when wide. Cards can span columns, cards in a row share a height, a row never has a hole (the cards of a short row widen in proportion to reach the edge) and rows grow to fill a tall window; low-priority cards show only when there is room. The column count and every span are packed on the server for each count and switched at run time by the width.

cards.doc: One entry per card in reading order: {"title", "note", "content", "span", "height", "priority", "align", "label"}. content is a node or a list of nodes (StatTile-free: use BigNumber, LineChart fill, BarChart fill, ProgressRing, Gauge fill, RankedList, KeyValueRow, a RowList embedded) placed in a box of exact width and the card's content height; inside it "@cardWidth" and "@cardHeight" are that box's size in dp. title is the card's heading (14 sp, one line), note a muted text at its end ("7 days"). span: columns it wants when there are that many (2 for a chart; default 1). height: dp its content needs (default 120); a row takes its tallest card. priority: the column count from which the card shows (default 1, always; 2 hides it on a phone). align: top (default), center or bottom, for content smaller than the row. label: what a screen reader says for the whole card

title.doc: The screen's heading (20 sp). Omit for no header

subtitle.doc: A muted line under the title: the period, the last update

minColumnWidth.doc: Narrowest a column gets: columns = (width - padding) / (minColumnWidth + gap), from 1 to maxColumns. 240 gives 1 column at 360, 2 at 640, 3 at 800 and 4 from about 1030 dp

gap.doc: Space between cards, across and down

grow.doc: Rows grow up to this many times their height to fill a window taller than the content (a desktop or tablet shows no empty band under the cards); 1 never grows. Past it the grid scrolls

width.doc: The width it has, when it is not the whole window (default windowWidth())

height.doc: The height it has, when it is not the whole window (default windowHeight())

headerEnd.doc: At the end of the header line: a Badge, a Chip, an IconButton

pitfalls: Content gets a box of exact width and height: a chart must fill it (fill: true, or fillMaxSize), and a component that needs its size given (RowList embedded, WorldMap) takes "@cardWidth" and "@cardHeight", which the grid replaces with that box's size. Nothing else in a card can read the grid's values

height is the content's height, title not included. Give each card what it needs at a phone's width: a row takes its tallest card and a 1-column phone gives each card exactly its own, so a KPI with height 120 beside a chart wastes nothing, but the same KPI alone on a phone is 120 dp tall
Do not put a StatTile or a Card in a card: they draw their own surface, so you get a tile inside a tile. Use BigNumber (and a Sparkline or TrendSparkline under it) for a KPI card

Order is reading order at every width: the grid does not reorder. Put the cards that should share a row next to each other (two KPIs, then a span-2 chart) and a span-2 chart after an even number of single cards, or its row-mate stretches to fill the hole it leaves

span is clamped to the columns there are, so a span-3 card is full width on 1 and 2 columns. A card that does not fit what is left of a row moves to the next row and the cards it leaves widen in proportion to their spans (two single cards in 3 columns get 1.5 each): no holes, but their edges no longer line up with the columns of other rows
priority 2 hides a card below 2 columns (a phone); it is still in the document. Keep at least one card at priority 1, and never hide the only place a number is shown

Rows grow up to grow times (1.3) to fill a taller window: content that fills (charts, rings) uses it, fixed content keeps its size and sits at align. A window much taller than the content still has space under the grid; set grow higher or add cards
Text does not shrink: the grid scrolls when there is not room, which is what a phone does; a widget-size window should not use it
